title: Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda Benefit Limits and Loan-to-Value Schedule
content:
# Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda — Benefit Limits and Loan-to-Value Schedule

This schedule of the Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda sets, for each of the six waivers, the figures that bound the GAP balance benefit: the loan-to-value cap, how financing above that cap reduces the benefit, the value the cap is measured against, the most the waiver pays, the part of the primary insurer's deductible the waiver covers, and the bases on which the payoff and the actual cash value (ACV) are taken.

## Schedule

| Waiver | Loan-to-value cap (fraction of the value basis) | Reduction for financing above the cap | Value the cap is measured against | Most paid on the GAP balance (USD) | Most paid as a fraction of the ACV settlement | Insurer deductible covered (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kessler GAP Waiver 125 | 1.25 (125 percent) | proportional reduction | MSRP or NADA retail value, by condition | 25000.00 | 1.0 (no such cap) | 0.00 |
| Kessler GAP Used Vehicle 140 | 1.4 (140 percent) | proportional reduction | NADA retail value | 35000.00 | 0.5 (50 percent) | 500.00 |
| Kessler GAP Waiver 150 | 1.5 (150 percent) | proportional reduction | MSRP or NADA retail value, by condition | 50000.00 | 1.0 (no such cap) | 500.00 |
| Kessler GAP Plus 150 | 1.5 (150 percent) | proportional reduction | MSRP or NADA retail value, by condition | 50000.00 | 1.0 (no such cap) | 1000.00 |
| Kessler GAP Plus 175 | 1.75 (175 percent) | proportional reduction | MSRP | 75000.00 | 1.0 (no such cap) | 1000.00 |
| Kessler GAP Commercial 130 | 1.3 (130 percent) | exclude excess amount | MSRP | 50000.00 | 0.5 (50 percent) | 0.00 |

Every waiver figures the payoff at loss on a simple interest daily basis (the lienholder's net payoff with simple interest accrued to the loss date), and takes as the ACV the primary insurer's settlement before its deductible.

## Meaning of each column

- **Loan-to-value cap** — a fraction of the vehicle value basis (1.25 means 125 percent); financing above it reduces the benefit.
- **Reduction for financing above the cap** — under proportional reduction the benefit is multiplied by the cap amount over the amount financed; under exclude excess amount the excess is subtracted.
- **Value the cap is measured against** — MSRP for new vehicles, NADA retail value for used vehicles, or MSRP or NADA retail value by condition.
- **Most paid on the GAP balance** — the dollar ceiling on the GAP balance benefit.
- **Most paid as a fraction of the ACV settlement** — a ceiling expressed against the primary insurer's ACV settlement; 1.0 means no such cap.
- **Insurer deductible covered** — the part of the primary insurer's deductible the waiver covers; any deductible above it is subtracted from the benefit.

## Reading the two ceilings together

Each waiver has two ceilings, a dollar figure and a fraction of the ACV settlement, and the lower of the two is the one that binds.

*Illustration (hypothetical figures):* under the Kessler GAP Used Vehicle 140, an ACV settlement of 41,800.00 gives a fraction ceiling of 0.5 times 41,800.00, that is 20,900.00, which is lower than the 35000.00 dollar ceiling, so 20,900.00 is the most the waiver pays on that loss. Under the Kessler GAP Waiver 150 the fraction is 1.0, so the same settlement leaves the 50000.00 dollar ceiling as the binding one.
